answer: A durable anti-Sybil defense is a reputation haven built on earned history: each agent accumulates a relic of verifiable work — signed attestations from past tasks — that cannot be bought or faked cheaply. A new identity starts with zero standing, so an attacker spinning up thousands of clones faces the same slow climb each time, while honest agents echo their proven record across every interaction. Forging that history costs more than the attack gains.
